top3.whyItMatters: The model drove results, so question costly custom agent machinery before funding more of it.

items.title: A playable Le Petit Prince game built by chaining AI tools
items.takeaway: Meng To says Sac made it with GPT Image 2.5, Tripo, and Opus 5.5 driving Blender and Unity.
items.soWhat: One maker chained image, 3D and coding models into a playable game and shared the prompts.

items.title: Musk: every missing input stalls a supercomputer build
items.takeaway: He endorsed a list running from land, permits and grid access to transformers, lathes and community politics.
items.soWhat: Compute plans depend on physical inputs, so check power and equipment lead times, not just chips.

items.title: Theo says Claude Agent SDK use drains 5-hour limits faster
items.takeaway: He says he confirmed the bug, weekly limits are unaffected, and he reported it to Anthropic. No Anthropic reply yet.
items.soWhat: Teams running agents on Claude subscriptions may hit limits sooner until Anthropic confirms or fixes it.

items.title: 1,008 mathematicians pledge to keep commercial AI out of their work
items.takeaway: 654 are in an AI-free caucus that does research without AI models; members won't publish AI-generated texts.
items.soWhat: Not every expert field will adopt AI, and some are now organizing to refuse it.

image.alt: Assoc. for Human Math: 1,008 mathematicians pledge to keep commercial AI out of their work

items.title: BIS: over half of AI firms' funding comes from other AI firms
items.takeaway: In 2021-2025, 55.2% of investment into AI firms came from AI firms; 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value also had supplier ties.
items.soWhat: BIS warns this circular money adds opacity and macro risk, so read AI revenue claims with care.

items.title: Study: elaborate agent harnesses add nothing over a minimal coding agent
items.takeaway: Same model, same time budget: open-source multi-agent setups did no better than one session with read, write and bash.
items.soWhat: On ML engineering tasks, the model mattered more than the machinery built around it.

items.title: US creative industries lost over 200k jobs in four years
items.takeaway: Politano says every digital arts subsector is shrinking while live entertainment grows; AI's exact share is hard to prove.
items.soWhat: The losses sit in digital work while live entertainment grows, a pattern worth watching in your workforce.

hotOnX.text: A fuller list of the limitations of supercomputer buildout. If anything is missing, however seemingly trivial, the compute doesn't work.
hotOnX.note: It frames AI compute as a physical supply problem, not just a chip problem.
